title: How do AI games get their characters?
author: InformationMajor4391
selftext:
Iam trying to make a game using AI (just for my own and seeing how far i can go) but it seems that i have reached a bottle neck, i want to put my custom made characters (enemies/allies) into the game but it seems impossible without knowing blender or having skills in these softwares(AIs dont do it themselves).  
I have seen alot of ppl share games and saying its 100% AI with great playable characters but idk where they get those characters?   
Anybody knows a way?

comments.author: HobiAI
comments.body: Buy Synty. They are cheap but the quality is high.

replies.author: cypryan_
replies.body: Can confirm. I also plan to use that!

comments.author: Live_Variety1645
comments.body: If you just had an A.I to look through the wast majority of the internet and prompt accordingly... hmm that would be too easy.. wouldnt it?

comments.author: newCesar3000
comments.body: AI can use blender usually you generate some references, front, side and back and let it cook.

replies.author: InformationMajor4391
replies.body: By "some reference" you mean whole meshed characters and rigged skeletons?

replies.author: Ferniclestix
replies.body: by reference they mean reference images, a few images from different sides for example like  a mugshot of what you want, front, side, back, maybe some detail features that kind of thing.

replies.author: Dryer-Algae
replies.body: Ask any ai to generate a front side and topdown image of a character for you, use it as template create the model yourself, get ai to make it or use a 3d modeling ai like tripo or meshy, if you just make a account on any of them and wait Abit the discounts start flowing

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body: I use Tripo and blender to polish.

comments.author: Ferniclestix
comments.body:
I mean you can buy stuff, you can teach yourself to make stuff, you can hire someone to make stuff or you could combine about 3 or 4 different tools to get AI to make stuff.

its doable but you have to basically figure out a work flow for it.  
some AI game tools exist that do this kind of thing out of the box.  
2d art is easiest.

you can literally scribble something ,send it to an ai and say, make this not look like a stick figure and go from there lol.

https://i.redd.it/rna6v5nxbl1i1.png

comments.author: PettyPotatoJuror
comments.body: My current workflow: Codex + Imagegen skill to create consistent turntable reference images of your character. Put those into 3D generation AI sub like Tripo or Meshy to generate the model, texture and basic rigging. Codex + Blender MCP for rig adjustments, animations, texture cleanup, export req for your destination platform.

comments.author: RecklessForm
comments.body:
Get a meshy sub and use that.   
Use CC0 models and tell claude to download them and rig them, very doable.   
Install blender and tell claude to use that.   
Tell Fable to do it, it'll just handle it.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: They're using asset packs, free repositories, or giving them AI keys to things like Tripo/Meshy/Higgsfield (higgsfield is just a central api bay that upcharges you for linking to a variety of other services.)

comments.author: TalkingHeadsVideo
comments.body: My workload is cursor for image prompt, Firefly for image(free from work acct), HI3D for 3d character, Character Creator AccuRig to rig, then import to Unreal

comments.body:
